title: summer-2026-applied-ml-bakeoff-decision-memo
body:
Summary:

This memo documents the results and recommendation from the Summer 2026 Applied ML model bakeoff. We compared four candidate model variants across our standard onboarding evaluation suite, new safety checks, and a human A/B preference study. The goal was to identify a model to promote as the new default candidate for hosted-chat and dedicated low-latency tiers for general-purpose assistants and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) flows.

Candidates evaluated:
- RW-13B-q4a (candidate v2026-02): Redwood-quantized 13B variant with custom kernel scheduling and prefix cache hooks.
- Llama2-13b-chat-fp16 (baseline v2025-11): upstream Llama2 chat model, FP16, our current baseline for many production routes.
- NeoX-20B-optimized (proto v1): larger open model we tested with trimmed attention and sequence-optimized kernels.
- Vicuna-33B-light (experiment): distilled 33B variant with aggressive filter and safety head.

Evaluation methodology:
- Automatic metrics: ROUGE-L on summarization prompts, exact-match and pass@1 for code snippets, perplexity on held-out instruction-following tasks.
- Safety & hallucination: automated factuality probe (checkpointed QA pairs), hallucination rate measured by model asserting false facts on ground-truth-labeled prompts, toxicity scoring with Perspective and internal classifiers.
- Latency & cost: p50/p95 token-generation latency measured on our staging Dedicated pool (A100-equivalent) and cost model of USD per 1k tokens based on throughput.
- Human preference study: 1,200 A/B pairs across tasks (summarization, multi-turn chat, RAG QA, code completion). Each pair judged by 3 raters with rubric (helpfulness, correctness, conciseness, tone).

Dataset / prompt sets used:
- SUM-SHORT-100: 100 short-article summarization prompts (news abstracts).
- SUM-LONG-50: 50 long-document summarization prompts (5-10 paragraphs).
- CODE-50: 50 code-completion and small-repair tasks sampled from internal playground.
- CHAT-200: multi-turn assistant conversations with persona and follow-ups.
- RAG-QA-200: retrieval-augmented QA using our standard 5-doc context.
- SAFETY-SMOKE-100: curated safety and bias probes focusing on edge-case harmful queries.

Key quantitative results (aggregated):
- Human win-rate (overall across tasks, higher is better):
  - RW-13B-q4a: 44.8%
  - Llama2-13b-chat-fp16: 33.2%
  - NeoX-20B-optimized: 15.7%
  - Vicuna-33B-light: 6.3%
- Hallucination rate (lower is better, measured on RAG-QA):
  - RW-13B-q4a: 6.1%
  - Llama2-13b-chat-fp16: 9.7%
  - NeoX-20B-optimized: 12.8%
  - Vicuna-33B-light: 10.6%
- Toxicity flagged (percentage of SAFETY-SMOKE triggers flagged by classifier):
  - RW-13B-q4a: 1.4%
  - Llama2-13b-chat-fp16: 2.9%
  - NeoX-20B-optimized: 3.6%
  - Vicuna-33B-light: 1.9%
- Latency p95 (ms/token) on Dedicated pool (lower is better):
  - RW-13B-q4a: 7.2 ms
  - Llama2-13b-chat-fp16: 6.6 ms
  - NeoX-20B-optimized: 9.8 ms
  - Vicuna-33B-light: 11.5 ms
- Cost per 1k output tokens (USD):
  - RW-13B-q4a: 0.48
  - Llama2-13b-chat-fp16: 0.62
  - NeoX-20B-optimized: 0.95
  - Vicuna-33B-light: 1.40

Interpretation / tradeoffs:
- Quality: RW-13B-q4a consistently wins in human preference across all major tasks. The win-rate margin is largest in RAG-QA and CHAT, where factuality and instruction-following matter most.
- Safety & hallucination: RW-13B-q4a shows a meaningful reduction in hallucination rate compared to our current baseline Llama2 v2025-11. Toxicity flags are lowest for RW-13B-q4a and Vicuna-33B-light; Vicuna has good safety numbers but loses heavily on helpfulness.
- Latency & cost: Llama2 baseline is marginally faster p95 but RW-13B-q4a’s p95 (7.2 ms) remains within our low-latency SLO for hosted routes. Cost-per-1k tokens is materially lower for RW-13B-q4a due to quantization and our runtime kernel tuning. NeoX and Vicuna are more expensive and slower on our runtime.

Leaderboards (ranked by composite score: 0.5*human-win-rate + 0.2*(1-hallucination) + 0.15*(1-toxicity) + 0.15*(cost-normalized)):
- 1) RW-13B-q4a
- 2) Llama2-13b-chat-fp16
- 3) NeoX-20B-optimized
- 4) Vicuna-33B-light

Win/Loss table (human A/B aggregated outcomes summarized as wins-losses-ties across 1,200 pairs):
RW-13B-q4a vs Llama2-13b-chat-fp16: 520-320-360
RW-13B-q4a vs NeoX-20B-optimized: 673-230-297
RW-13B-q4a vs Vicuna-33B-light: 789-112-299
Llama2-13b-chat-fp16 vs NeoX-20B-optimized: 412-360-428
Llama2-13b-chat-fp16 vs Vicuna-33B-light: 541-210-449

Regression notes vs baseline (Llama2 v2025-11):
- RW-13B-q4a shows a +11.6 percentage point uplift in overall human win-rate and reduces hallucination by ~3.6 percentage points.
- Slight increase in average latency (p95 +0.6 ms) but still within SLO for hosted low-latency tier.
- No new safety class regressions detected in the SAFETY-SMOKE suite; false-positive safe refusals increased slightly on one prompt subtype (political persuasion edge-cases) — tracked as follow-up.

Recommendation and rollout plan:
- Approve RW-13B-q4a (candidate v2026-02) as the primary candidate for staged rollout to Hosted API general assistant route and Dedicated low-latency reserved pools.
- Canary plan (2 weeks):
  - 5% traffic in Hosted on canary route A with monitoring hooks for latency, error rates, hallucination alerts (automated RAG checks), and human-reported quality via sample flagging.
  - Dedicated: deploy as optional model flavor for new Dedicated customers and enable as default for new internal test projects.
- Rollback / stop criteria:
  - User-facing hallucination alert rate exceeds baseline by >50% for 24h, or
  - Latency p95 increases beyond our SLO by >25% for 12h, or
  - Multiple independent safety regressions from human review across different prompt categories within 48h.

Action items & owners:
- eng-applied-ml: finalize quantization profile and shipping image (owner: Priya Desai, due: 2026-03-02).
- infra/serving-runtime: prepare canary capacity and tracing hooks (owner: Liam Chen, due: 2026-03-05).
- product/hosted-api: update route metadata and cost table (owner: Sofia Martinez, due: 2026-03-08).
- security/research: deeper safety sweep on political persuasion subtype and multilingual fringe (owner: Marco Alvarez, due: 2026-03-10).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Multi-lingual generalization: our bakeoff was English-only — need a smaller focused bakeoff in Spanish, Mandarin, and Japanese before enterprise-wide promotion.
- Long-form summarization: candidate shows small regressions on SUM-LONG-50; run targeted prompt engineering and reevaluate.
- Fine-grain cost modeling for Dedicated GPU variants with autoscaling bursts.

Appendix (brief):
- Full per-task breakdowns, raw human annotations, and model logits archived at linked artifact GH-PR-4682.
- Evaluation scripts and prompt sets are in the repo under /evals/2026/summer-bakeoff.

Conclusion:
RW-13B-q4a is the strongest balance of quality, safety, latency, and unit cost for our immediate use cases. Recommend staged promotion with the canary plan above and the listed tracked follow-ups.

Evidence and data included in attached CSVs and Confluence logs (linked).

Prepared by: Priya Desai (eng-applied-ml)
Reviewed by: Liam Chen, Sofia Martinez, Marco Alvarez
